supersedes.git: dd7fa204 (build_dock.py and this file as released for A1)
supersedes.why: in the real Brain sit (funnel-concept, --model asbuilt --manifest current) the A1 leaf tip lay behind the pad in all 46 runs, even with the robot exactly centred: A1 never charges
supersedes.approved: Shawn 2026-11-20: "导轨倒是可以 ... 看看能不能把它对准坐下去", then "出 CAD" on funnel-concept/concept-sheet.png (DESIGN-CONTRACT.json)

frame: x forward, y left, z above the floor with the robot seated (the A1 frame); the concept sheet and the sims use frame D, D x = x + 3.0

needs.N1: a seated robot's two pads must each meet one sprung contact: + under the y +9 pad, - under the y -9 pad
needs.N2: the contacts must be held as Keystone intends (5209 body pressed into a housing groove), with nothing printed that bends
needs.N3: the robot must be stopped in x so its pads land over the leaves
needs.N4: the charger plug must enter a panel jack wired to the two contacts with short soldered wires
needs.N5: the dock must stay where it is put
needs.N6: a robot that sits down off to one side must be pushed sideways until each pad is over its own leaf
needs.N7: a robot that sits down too far back must slide forward onto the stop, never hang on the dock
needs.N8: the guidance must never touch the legs or feet in stand, sit and stand-up

premises.P-SEAT: seated backpack bottom flat at z 10.9 (battery-v2 rev B, pad STL z -46 + 56.9); the sim Brain sit puts the pads at 10.2 with -1.9 deg pitch and pushes the backpack against the stop (funnel-concept)
premises.P-PADS: Keystone 615 pad faces 7.1 x 8.7 at x -73.85..-65.15, y +-9 (battery-v2 build/parts/contact_pad_*-world.stl); plus = y +9
premises.P-BACK: backpack back face x -75.55; the two low cap screws (M2 x 6, pan head 4.0 x 1.6 proud) at y +-9, z 18.0 seated
premises.P-TIER: backpack lower tier y -25.3..+21.8 from seated z 10.9 to about 42 (frame + cap STL sections); the wider wings start above
premises.P-SIM: funnel-concept/checks/results.json and the B1 recheck checks/b1check.jsonl: tolerances, rail clearance to legs and feet
premises.P-5209: Keystone 5209 (M65p15): 0.30 bronze, body 14.0 x 10.0 (wings) / 7.0, leaf 7.0 wide, 10.9 REF, free 7.6 MIN, tab 5.0 x 7.0 jogged 1.6; press fit into a housing groove; working travel about 3 mm (M65p36)
premises.P-JACK: Same Sky PJ-005A rev 1.09: bushing 7.94 x 5.7, flange 10.8, housing 10.0, 15.5 to lug ends, nut 10.8 AF x 2.0, washer 10.9 x 0.5; centre-pin lug 3.8 above the axis, sleeve lug on the axis, shunt lug 4.4 below

features.what: two solid rails x -80..-62 (D -77..-59): guide faces at y +24.8 and -28.3 (3.0 outside the lower tier), vertical from the floor to z 12.5, 60 deg lead-in to z 24.0, 2.5 flat top, vertical outer face (y +33.94 / -37.44)
features.why: the leaves alone take a sideways error of about -3..0 mm; the rails catch the lower tier's side walls (the only flat vertical surfaces low enough to guide before the pads touch) and push the robot sideways to within 3 mm, the sim's y window grows to -15..0 mm
features.simpler: wider leaves or pads: the leaves sit 18 mm apart and a wider leaf would reach the other pad; a floor groove for the feet: the feet lift off during the sit
features.validation: rail_section_probe in build.json matches the approved section at 8 heights on each rail; DESIGN-CONTRACT.json bounds PASS; B1 sit recheck on the built pieces (checks/b1check.jsonl)
features.change_when: the backpack's lower tier width or the pad positions change, or the robot hangs on a lead-in in a real sit

features.what: stop face x -76.5 (D -73.5: the whole dock 3.0 mm forward of where A1 sat in the sim), the 5209 bodies 2.5 mm forward of the stop face (x -74.0..-60.0, groove closed end -60.0); 2.5 mm of empty groove behind each body
features.why: the sim seat is 1.9 deg nose-up and the tail meets the stop, which puts the pad 2-3 mm forward of A1's nominal; with the leaves 2.5 mm forward the compressed tip (x -69.88) lies near the pad centre in every checked pose (margin 3.8-4.1 mm)
features.simpler: A1 unchanged: tip behind the pad in all 46 sim runs
features.validation: leaf_under_pad in build.json: margin >= 0.5 at the nominal seat, against the stop and at the sim's seat height; contract bounds on the contact bodies
features.change_when: the real robot's seated pad position on the dock is measured and differs from the sim by more than 1 mm

features.what: 45 deg plane rising rearward from the stop face's top edge (x -76.5, z 12.5) over the stop wall and the tower's side walls, meeting the tower top at x -86.0; the stop wall is 11.1 thick (9.5 of slope, then 1.6 flat at the tower top's z 22, so the centre post ends square); the insertion slots open upward through it. A 3.2 wall gave a 0.4 mm knife edge, and capping it with a flat at z 14.1 made a ledge the robot hung on (first B1 recheck case)
features.why: A1 had a flat relief ledge at z 14.6 and a flat tower top at 22: a robot 3-6 mm back hung on them in the sim; a slope turns a landing on top into a slide onto the stop. The plane starts at 12.5, not the concept's 14.6, because the low cap screw heads (not in the concept sim's hull) would rest on a plane from 14.6 with the backpack against the stop
features.simpler: A1's relief ledge: robots hang on it; a taller stop: leaves a flat top to hang on
features.validation: lead_in_probe in build.json matches the plane at 6 points; screw_heads_vs_lead_in gaps >= 0.3 (measured 1.76 or more incl. +-3 mm side play); the B1 recheck carries the screw heads in the backpack hull
features.change_when: the cap screws move or get countersunk, or a real sit hangs on the slope

features.what: rails end at x -62 (D -59), top at z 24, outer faces inside |y| 38; plate bridge under the rails x -80..-62
features.why: the left foot comes down at D x -51 at the end of the stand-up, and the legs never come behind D x -40 while standing or sitting; the long-rail concept variant (to D -50) touched the legs in 8 runs
features.validation: legs_vs_dock in build.json (sim leg envelope over stand, sit, stand-up: nearest 17.9 mm); the B1 recheck measures rail clearance per run; contract bounds
features.change_when: the stand-up motion or the foot placement changes

features.what: 2.0 mm plate x -107.9..-55, y -20..20, z 0..2, plus a 2.0 mm bridge x -80..-62 under both rails (y -37.44..33.94)
features.why: ties the contact block, the stop tower and the rails into one part so their relation is fixed; the underside takes foam tape or Dual Lock (N5 has no printed feature)
features.simpler: rails as separate parts taped down: their spacing would be set by hand each time
features.validation: one closed body; bounds in build.json; legs_vs_dock

features.why: carries the two grooves at the pad positions; top 2.9 mm under the seated pads so only the leaves touch them; front face 1.75 in front of the leaf opening
features.simpler: contacts glued to the plate: Keystone's mount is a press groove
features.validation: block top 8.0 <= 8.5; zero robot overlap in all three seated poses
features.change_when: the pads move or the seat height changes

features.what: two grooves along x at y +-9: 10.50 wide, 0.40 tall, floor z 6.0, from the stop face to the closed end at x -60.0
features.why: press fit as Keystone intends: thickness print_fit press class with the horizontal adder (+0.05/side, two 0.2 layers over the 0.30 bronze); width locating, horizontal (+0.25/side). The closed front end takes the drag the pad puts on the leaf while the robot sits down
features.simpler: a groove open at the front: the drag at every sit would walk the body out
features.validation: fit_check.py FITS.json OK; zero overlap between the dock and the contact envelopes
features.change_when: a bench print shows the 0.40 slot too loose or too tight; write the result into PRINT-FIT.md the same day
features.known_boundary: print_fit's press class is written for vertical pins; a horizontal sheet-metal press slot has no bench evidence yet

features.what: 7.30 wide openings in the block top over each groove, from the rear to 0.75 past the leaf root (x -59.25); lips 1.6 wide x 1.6 tall over the wings
features.why: the leaf rises through it to the pad; locating fit (+0.15/side, vertical walls) keeps 1.35 mm of each wing under its lip
features.simpler: fully open groove top: nothing would hold the body down

features.what: tower front wall x -87.6..-76.5, |y| <= 17; stop face x -76.5 from the plate to z 12.5 on three posts (centre |y| < 3.5, outer |y| 14.5..17) between the slots
features.why: places the backpack so the pads land over the leaves; the back face meets it over z 10.2..12.5
features.simpler: no stop: the robot would have to place an 8.7 mm pad within a few mm by dead reckoning
features.validation: contract bound x_max -76.5 on features/stop_wall; zero overlap with the robot against the stop

features.what: two 11.0 wide slots through the stop wall at y +-9 from z 3.8, open to the top, running on into the block to 0.6 past the body's rear end (x -73.4)
features.why: the contact slides in from inside the tower, leaf root first (loose class, horizontal); the floor at 3.8 passes the tab whichever way its 1.6 jog goes; the slot runs into the block because the body sits 2.5 forward of the stop and the tab lies in the block's first 2.5 mm. Open-topped because the lead-in plane runs below A1's gable eave (the gable's remains were 0.2-0.9 mm slivers); the low cap screw heads sit over the slots at every seated pose
features.simpler: A1's gabled slot: slivers under the lead-in
features.validation: zero overlap with the contact envelopes; wall check passes
features.change_when: the contact part or its insertion direction changes

features.what: hollow tower x -107.9..-76.5, |y| <= 17, side walls 2.0 and rear wall 2.5 to z 22 behind the 11.1 stop wall, open top
features.why: holds the jack on the x axis and shelters the tab-to-lug wires; the open top gives the soldering iron access
features.simpler: jack in the block: no room under z 8 for a 10.8 flange and its lugs
features.validation: jack envelope overlaps 0; soldering_iron_access: a 3.5 mm radius barrel straight down and 30 deg back onto both lugs meets no material

features.what: tower interior x -105.4..-87.6, |y| <= 15, from the plate up, open at the top
features.why: contacts go in and lugs are soldered from above
features.simpler: closed tower: the jack lugs could not be reached

features.what: 8.44 hole in the rear wall on the x axis at y 0, z 10, teardrop tip +z
features.why: PJ-005A bushing 7.94 through a 2.5 mm panel, nut and washer outside, plug from behind; locating fit with the horizontal adder; teardrop because the axis lies in the layer plane (PRINT-FIT Teardrops)
features.validation: fit_check.py jack-hole OK (tip +z in the print pose); 0.7 mm of bushing left past the nut

removed.what: 1.5 mm recess across the stop face from z 14.6 to the top
removed.why_removed: it was the ledge a robot 3-4 mm back hung on in the sim; F3's lead-in replaces it, and the screw heads now clear the lead-in (and sit over the open slots) instead
removed.do_not_restore_unless: the screw heads stand further proud or move off y +-9
